task: Write one sentence of your own using the word adroit. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know adroit should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The sitter proved adroit with the twins, trading the scissors they'd found for bubble wands before either could protest.
Competent is milder than adroit — competent handling gets the tray to the table without applause or incident; adroit adds grace and judgment the moment the tray tips.
Nimble is quick and light on its feet, but it is only the speed; adroit adds the judgment — the right move, made smoothly, at the tricky moment.

Slick is smooth skill with showmanship in it — the move announces its own polish, and the word often carries a raised eyebrow. Adroit is clean of that suspicion: clever, graceful handling praised without irony. A slick answer makes you check your wallet; an adroit one makes you admire the save.

Resourceful praises making do — clever use of whatever happens to be at hand, with nothing said about grace. Adroit praises the handling itself: a tricky object or moment managed smoothly and well. A resourceful camper improvises a tent pole; an adroit host settles the argument before anyone notices a rescue.
